paper_summary: Doctoral thesis (Afolabi, Durban University of Technology) on epoxy syntactic foam composites (SFC) made by open resin casting/stir mixing with degassing of DGEBA epoxy (LR 20 / LH281) filled with T60 hollow glass microspheres (true density 0.6 g/cc, radius ratio 0.9141) at 5-25 vol%, used both as heterogeneous (as-received, whole size distribution) filler and as four sieved homogeneous size classes AA 20-24, BB 25-44, CC 45-49 and DD 50-60 um. Density, tensile, flexural, impact, hardness, water absorption, buoyancy, TGA and DMA properties were measured; tensile modulus peaked at 4.63 GPa (EPT60-15) and flexural strength at 118 MPa (EPT60-25), both far above the neat epoxy, while the homogeneous size-classified foams generally showed lower moduli than the heterogeneous ones. The SFC was then used as the core of hybrid sandwich panels with kenaf and/or glass fibre face sheets (KK, GG, GK, KG), whose density, tensile, flexural, edgewise-compression, shear, water-absorption, buoyancy and acoustic properties were measured and compared with series/parallel/Hirsch models.

extraction_notes: Units: all moduli converted GPa -> MPa; tan delta values in Table 9.7 are tabulated as 'x10^3' and were divided by 1000; volume fractions converted from % to fractions; sandwich porosity (void) % converted to a fraction in matrix_porosity_fraction. particle_volume_fraction for the sieved homogeneous foams uses the nominal 5-25 vol% loading; particle_true_density_g_cc uses the size-class powder density rho_d of Table 4.2 (OO 0.600, AA 0.7548, BB 0.7286, CC 0.7083, DD 0.5529 g/cc) and particle_mean_diameter_um the measured mean diameter d of the same table (OO 39.26, AA 29.62, BB 30.86, CC 29.40, DD 55.04 um); Table 3.1 quotes the manufacturer's nominal T60 true density of 0.6 g/cc for all sizes. SFC bulk densities per composition are only shown graphically (Figs. 5.2-5.4), so measured_density_g_cc is left null for all SFC records even though the tables report specific (density-normalised) properties; only the sandwich panels have tabulated densities (Table 8.1). Table 7.2 restates the present-work flexural moduli as 2359/3485/3728/3931/4292/5752 MPa, which differ slightly from the 2.4/3.5/3.7/3.9/4.3/4.8 GPa of Table 7.1; the Table 7.1 values (consistent with the narrative text) were used. Table 7.2 also lists neat-epoxy flexural strength as 53.3 MPa vs 53.5 MPa in Table 7.1; 53.5 was used. Charpy impact results (neat epoxy 84.57 kJ/m2, EPT60-5 113.12 kJ/m2, remaining compositions given only as percentage increases that are inconsistent with the quoted peak value) are reported per unit area, which cannot be converted to the schema's MJ/m3 energy_absorption field, so no impact records were created. TGA decomposition temperatures (Tables 9.1-9.2), Tg/Tmax (Table 9.4), loss modulus E'' (Tables 9.5-9.6), Barcol hardness (Tables 10.1-10.2), buoyancy force (Tables 10.7-10.8) and acoustic sound level/pressure (Tables 10.9-10.10) have no corresponding schema field and were omitted. The HGM volume fraction of the syntactic-foam core used in the sandwich panels is never stated; the modelling tables (8.7/8.8) use SFC modulus 4.57 GPa and strength 66.73 MPa, i.e. the EPT60-20 heterogeneous foam, so core particle_volume_fraction is left null and noted in microstructure_notes. Sandwich rows carry the fibre face-sheet description in additional_fillers; their properties are panel-level, not core-level. Rows from Tables 6.2 and 7.2 quoting other authors are marked secondary and carry the citation in sample_label; the series/parallel/Hirsch predictions of Tables 8.7-8.8 are marked model. Test 'strain rate' quoted in the thesis (50 mm/mm tensile, 5 mm/mm flexural) is not a strain rate, so strain_rate_per_s is left null; tests were at room temperature (taken as 25 C).
